title: HYPOChLorous Acid TEsting Studies: Secondary PERITONITIS
summary: Hypoclates:Peritonitis investigates which irrigation fluid administered during and after surgery for secondary peritonitis (abdominal inflammation, e.g., due to perforation of a hollow organ) is most suitable to prevent surgical site infections. Surgery for secondary peritonitis is inherently a high-risk procedure for wound infections due to the already prevailing inflammation. In this study, we compare two different irrigation approaches: the previous standard method with isotonic saline solution (single irrigation during surgery) and prolonged irrigation with Granudacyn® – a medical product containing hypochlorous acid (HOCl) as its active ingredient, which is already successfully used in wound care. The main objective is to determine which irrigation method is superior in preventing wound infections. The results of this study could help improve future treatment recommendations for surgery in secondary peritonitis and thus optimize patient outcomes. Additionally, it is one of the first studies to examine the potential positive efficacy of hypochlorous acid in surgical site infection prophylaxis in an actual clinical context.
conditions: Infection following a procedure, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of clinical routine data from approximately 100 patients who were operated on from September to November 2025 based on the diagnosis of secondary peritonitis and were lavaged with isotonic solution during the procedure.

Prospective analysis of clinical routine data from approximately 100 patients who were operated on from December 2025 to February 2026 based on the diagnosis of secondary peritonitis and received extended lavage (single intraoperative lavage and three days of postoperative irrigation via a drainage)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned surgical treatment of secondary peritonitis
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, previous organ transplantation, inability to administer antibiotics
